risks.risk: Whether the compressor/refrigeration system is actually working (could be dead, weak, or leaking).
risks.proof: A short video of the freezer plugged in with the compressor running and the temperature dropping (or an IR thermometer showing cold interior after 30–60 minutes).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed working (worst case: treat as needs repair / not cooling).

risks.risk: Whether it holds temperature for the claimed duration (insulation/door seal condition).
risks.proof: Photo/video of door gasket condition plus a temperature log (e.g., thermometer reading inside after a set time).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as average/unknown cooling performance (worst case: not meeting the 120-hour claim).

risks.risk: Electrical compatibility/safety (low-voltage claim may be incorrect; also check for faulty wiring).
risks.proof: A photo of the rating plate (voltage/Hz) and a test showing it runs on the buyer’s available supply (with a stabilizer if needed).
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming standard operation only and possible electrical issues (worst case: may not run reliably).

risks.risk: Age/condition and possible dents/rust affecting resale value.
risks.proof: More photos: sides, back, underside, and close-ups of dents/rust and the lid seal.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at a conservative condition level based on exterior-only visibility.

proof_requests: Rating plate photo (brand/model, voltage/Hz, refrigerant info) and serial number if available.
Video showing it plugged in: compressor start + interior temperature dropping (or thermometer reading).
Close-up photos of the door gasket/seal and latch.
Photos of the back/side vents and any rust/dents.
response.reason: The photo supports the capacity and the '120 hours cooling retention' sticker text, but there is no remote proof it is actually working or that it meets the cooling claim; the key price driver is functional performance.
